properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Gila County in east central Arizona...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 900 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks and normally dry washes is imminent or
occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 553 PM MST, river gauges along Cherry Creek and Cibecue Creek
report that water levels have crested, however elevated flow
remains. Flooding is ongoing across the warned area.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Carrizo Creek, Cibecue Creek, Cherry Creek, Salt River Draw, and
Salome Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Cibecue, Young, Forest Lakes, Sierra Ancha Wilderness, Cibeque
Falls, and Valley View Point.
- This includes State Route 288 between mile markers 294 and 298...
and between mile markers 307 and 311.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Airplane Flat Campground, Colcord Ridge Campground, Upper Canyon
Creek Campground and Valentine Ridge Campground.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Cibeque Falls.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

properties.areaDesc: Palm Beach, FL
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 7:50PM EST until November 1 at 9:15PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
At 750 PM EST, The public reported flash flooding in communities near
Military Trail road, with water starting to enter homes. Roads and
streets nearby Okeechobee Road and Military trail are reported to be
impassable. Between 7 and 10 inches of rain have fallen. The expected
rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts
of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash
flooding.

SOURCE...Public reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
West Palm Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, Riviera Beach, North Palm
Beach, Lake Park, Haverhill, Cloud Lake, Schall Circle, Port Of
Palm Beach, Golden Lakes, Lake Belvedere Estates, Royal Palm
Estates, President Donald J. Trump International Airport, Downtown
West Palm Beach, Gun Club Estates, Mangonia Park, Glen Ridge,
Lakeside Green and Cypress Lakes.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.areaDesc: Gila, AZ; Maricopa, AZ; Pinal, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 5:48PM MST until November 1 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Gila County in east central Arizona...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 800 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 536 PM MST, Heavy rainfall from earlier today continues to
result in excess runoff in area creeks. Gages along Pinto Creek
and Pinal Creek show continued elevated flows that will continue
downstream to Roosevelt Lake. Flooding is already occurring in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Roosevelt, Tonto National Monument, Roosevelt Dam, Apache Lake,
Roosevelt Estates and Inspiration.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Yavapai, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 5:45PM MST until November 1 at 11:45PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1145 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks and normally dry washes is imminent or
occurring. Roads are closed and impassable due to flooding. Deadly
flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 545 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges continued
to indicate heavy rain over the warned area. Stream gauges also
continued to report elevated flow in Big Chino Wash, Williamson
Valley Wash, Ash Creek, and Sycamore Creek. Flooding is ongoing
in the warned area. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Ash Creek, Cienega Creek, Granite Creek,  Willow Creek, Agua Fria
River, Lynx Creek, Little Ash Creek, Williamson Valley Wash,
Walnut Creek, Verde River, Ash Fork Draw, and Big Chino Wash.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Prescott Valley, Chino Valley, Williamson Valley, Paulden, Ash
Fork, Agua Fria National Monument, Drake, Kaibab Estates West,
Flower Pot, Perkinsville, Yavapai County Fairgrounds, Dugas,
Crookton, Cedar Mill, Fain Lake, Granite Mountain Wilderness and
Woodchute Mountain.
- This includes the following highways...
Interstate 40 between mile markers 132 and 147. State Route 69
between mile markers 284 and 290. Business Interstate 40 near
mile marker 146. Interstate 17 between mile markers 269 and 280.
State Route 89 between mile markers 322 and 363. State Route 89A
between mile markers 322 and 335.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Powell Springs Campground, Texaco Hillside RV Campground and
Mountainview Park.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

thunderstorms extending from 7 miles southeast of La Cueva to near
Villanueva, moving northeast at 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Las Vegas, Wagon Mound, Watrous, Valmora, Storrie Lake State Park,
Sapello, Montezuma, Romeroville, Trujillo and Tecolote.

This includes the following highways...
State Road 518 between Mile Markers 1 and 22. Interstate 25 between
Mile Markers 321 and 365...and between Mile Markers 366 and 399.
State Road 104 between Mile Markers 1 and 35.
properties.instruction:

weather conditions.

stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

properties.areaDesc: Maricopa, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 5:34PM MST until November 1 at 7:45PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 745 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 530 PM MST, gauge reports indicated Cave Creek remains above
Action stage with the current stage above 7 feet. Flooding is
already occurring in the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Cave Creek, Carefree, Desert Mountain, Camp Creek and Seven
Springs.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

between mile markers 267 and 276. State Route 87 southbound
between mile markers 241 and 251. State Route 87 between mile
markers 230 and 292.

Campground, Sharp Creek Campground, Rim Campground, Promontory

Rim Campground, Rumsey Park, Green Valley Park, Bear Canyon Lake
Recreation Area, Willow Springs Lake Recreation Area, Sardine

This includes the following swimming holes...
Horton Springs, Water Wheel Falls, Ellison Creek Cascades, All
swimming holes and waterfalls on Fossil Creek, Tonto Creek
Waterfalls, Fossil Creek Dam "The Toilet Bowl" and Indian Maiden
Falls.

properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Moenkopi Wash in Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 100 AM MST Monday.

* At 458 PM MST, a gauge on the Moenkopi Wash reported a rise above
action stage from heavy rain in the Moenkopi Wash basin. Further
rises are expected, with water levels expected to exceed major
flood stage. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Moenkopi Wash.

* For Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City:
At 4:45pm MST the stage was 26.0 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 29.45 feet is expected at 5:00am MST Monday.
Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in
lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Moenkopi.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Fivemile Wash, Hamblin Wash, Begashibito Wash and Moenkopi Wash.
properties.instruction:

muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 1 at 3:56PM PST until November 2 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 4:55PM MST until November 1 at 6:30PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Graham County in southeastern Arizona...
Greenlee County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 630 PM MST.

* At 455 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated 1
to 2 inches of rain had fallen across eastern Graham and Greenlee
county earlier today, with light to moderate showers persisting
across the area. Rainfall runoff on already saturated soils will
result in swift water runoff... resulting in a persisting threat
for flash flooding.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Safford, Clifton, Solomon, Morenci, San Jose, Safford Regional
Airport, Roper Lake State Park, Hannagan Meadow, Blue, Duncan,
York, Franklin, Guthrie, Three Way, Rose Peak, Point-Of-Pines and
Swift Trail Junction.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...

properties.areaDesc: Gila, AZ; Yavapai, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 4:52PM MST until November 1 at 9:30PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues along the
Verde River.

* WHERE...The Verde River from Clarkdale to Camp Verde to Horseshoe
Reservoir.

* WHEN...Until 930 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Further rises in the water levels of already flooded
creeks and normally dry washes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 447 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
an area of very heavy rainfall across the Verde River Basin.
Water levels at Clarkdale have risen above major flood stage,
with water beginning to rise at the guage near Camp Verde.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Verde River.
- For the Verde River at Clarkdale:
At 4:00pm the stage was 22.47 feet.
Flood Stage is 12.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest is expected later this evening.
Impacts:
At 15.0 feet: Flooding of River Day Use Area on Owl Road at Dead
Horse Ranch State Park. Flooding of ECO Farm, Rio Verde RV Park,
and homes along Bates Road and Rocking Chair Ranch Road in
Cottonwood begins.
At 20.0 feet: Widespread flooding of low-lying homes and roadways
along the Verde River.

- For the Verde River near Camp Verde:
At 4:00pm the stage was 12.52 feet.
Flood Stage is 17.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 24.33 feet is expected at 1:00am Monday.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Water begins to flood sites and lower road at Verde
River RV Resort and Cottages.
At 19.0 feet: Flooding begins in Horseshoe Bend area just
upstream of Camp Verde. Several properties and homes begin to
flood along the Verde River downstream in Camp Verde to Beasley
Flat area.
At 21.0 feet: Inundation of homes along the Verde River from the
Horseshoe Bend area upstream of Camp Verde to the Beasley Flat
area.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Cottonwood, Camp Verde, Verde Village, Clarkdale, Middle Verde,
Verde Lakes, Mountain View Estates, Bignotti, Bridgeport, Childs
Power Plant, Dead Horse Ranch State Park, Fort Verde State
Historic Park, Tuzigoot National Monument, Rockin' River Ranch
State Park, Chalk Mountain and Sunset Mountain. - This includes
the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Red-Tail Hawk Loop Campground, Quail Loop Campground, Raven Loop
Campground, Blackhawk Loop Campground and Cooper's Hawk Loop
Campground.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Avalanche Advisory issued November 1 at 4:51PM MST by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
SABCO

THE FOLLOWING MESSAGE IS TRANSMITTED AT THE REQUEST OF THE
COLORADO AVALANCHE INFORMATION CENTER.

...A SPECIAL AVALANCHE ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 4:30 PM SUNDAY
UNTIL 4:30 PM MONDAY...

*WHAT...Avalanche conditions are dangerous above treeline.
*WHERE...San Juan Mountains
*WHEN... From 4:30 PM Sunday until 4:30 PM Monday.
*IMPACTS... Backcountry travelers can easily trigger dangerous avalanches large enough to bury a human.
*PRECAUTION/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS... A potent winter storm increases avalanche danger Sunday into Monday. Rain, snow, and wind will cause natural avalanches above treeline. Check the forecast at www.colorado.gov/avalanche.



Beyer

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 3:52PM MST until November 1 at 10:30PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Paria River in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 1030 PM MST Sunday.

* At 352 PM MST, a river gauge on the Paria River reported a rapid
rise from heavy rain over the Paria River drainage basin. Flood
waters will proceed down the Paria River drainage this evening
reaching Lees Ferry between about 8 to 10 PM MST.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Paria River.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Paria River.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lees Ferry and Vermilion Cliffs National Monument.

This includes the Colorado River near mile marker 0.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Lees Ferry Camp Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Colorado River and Paria River.
properties.instruction:
Get out of the Paria River slot canyon! Flood waters will flow down
the Paria River, reaching the confluence with the Colorado River at
Lees Ferry around 8:00 to 10:00 PM MST.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Get out of washes and creeks if you are camping or hiking! Flooding
is occurring or imminent and will inundate creeks and washes.

underpasses.

...

At 2:45pm the stage was 13.93 feet.

water crossings closed.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 1 at 2:25PM PST until November 1 at 6:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents.

* WHERE...San Francisco, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern
Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 PM PST this
evening. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from late tonight
through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) on
Sunday 11/01 at 3:59 PM. These predictions include up to 1.5
ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas

currents.

Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 PM PST this

through Tuesday evening.

infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.

areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

tide is expected to be 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) on

flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.

property.

alternative route.

the possibility of the advisory being upgraded to a warning.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 2:09PM MST until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central, northwest, and west central New
Mexico, including the following areas, in north central New Mexico,
Far Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands and
Tusas Mountains Including Chama. In northwest New Mexico, Chuska
Mountains and Northwest Plateau. In west central New Mexico, San
Francisco River Valley, Southwest Mountains, West Central
Highlands, West Central Mountains and West Central Plateau.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Another round of widespread rainfall is expected today into
Monday with rainfall amounts generally between 1 and 2 inches
near and west of the Continental Divide, except near 3 inches in
favored upslope regions of the Tusas Mountains near Chama. This
rainfall will occur over very saturated soils which will increase
runoff. These are also areas that are still recovering from the
last flood event. River rises are likely and some rivers may
flood. If river flooding materializes, it will likely continue
into Monday evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 1 at 2:57PM EST until November 2 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 7 feet
in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Saint Lucie and Coastal Martin Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 PM EST Monday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet.

* WHERE...North facing reefs of Yap.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM ChST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated long-period north swell, emanating
from distant Typhoon In-fa, is moving through the region,
generating hazardous surf along north facing reefs of Yap. To
the southwest of Yap, overnight buoy data from Babeldaob, Palau,
showed a sharp increase in 12 to 14 second swell from the
northeast, with combined seas at least one foot above model
guidance. This was an indicator that the long-period swell may
be arriving slightly sooner than indicated by guidance,
sufficient to produce hazardous surf of 9 feet, potentially
reaching 10 feet tonight, along north facing reefs of Yap. For
Yap, the swell is expected to be north-northeast, and about 1 to
2 feet higher than that expected for Palau, where north-facing
surf looks to remain just below 9 feet.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 1 at 10:29AM PST until November 2 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated
surf expected. Minor tidal overflow during high tides.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Minor flood impacts are possible during high tides
with water flowing over normally dry sand and to lower parking
lots or paths. Moderate beach erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Additional flood impacts are likely into
next weekend with tides reaching 7 ft as early as Friday. Tides
will peak over the weekend into early next week 7.0-7.8 ft.
Elevated surf may increase flood impacts during this time,
especially across west to northwest facing beaches. Reminder,
tides mentioned have been corrected to reflect the most recent
trends in actual tide observations.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 11:22AM MST until November 1 at 10:00PM MST by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...In Southwest New Mexico, Grant County, northern Hidalgo
County, and western Sierra County. This includes Silver City,
Lordsburg, Gila, and other surrounding communities. This includes
the Gila and upper Mimbres watersheds.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may become flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Pacific frontal boundary will move through New Mexico this
afternoon, bringing widespread showers and thunderstorms to much
of western New Mexico. Storms will be capable of heavy rain and
training, which will lead to localized flash flooding. High soil
saturation due to recent rains will cause runoff to occur more
quickly.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 1 at 1:20PM EST until November 3 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Tuesday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 PM EST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 10 feet in the surf zone
and dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...West and north facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 PM ChST Monday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated, long-period, northwest swell from
Typhoon In-fa will continue to produce hazardous surf and a high
risk of rip currents along west and north facing reefs through

feet is expected to diminish below hazardous levels, becoming 6
to 8 feet tonight. However, if the long-period swell energy
remains elevated longer than expected, then the High Surf
Advisory and High Rip Current Risk Statement may be extended
once more.

should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions.

the current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline.
If unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Pearl River, MS
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 6:02AM CST until November 2 at 6:00PM CST by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Mississippi...

West Hobolochitto Creek Near McNeil affecting Pearl River County.

For the West Hobolochitto Creek...including McNeil...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...West Hobolochitto Creek near McNeil.

* WHEN...From early this morning to Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, North Beech Road and Palestine Road in
Picayune will be impassable. Several homes will be flooded in
vicinity of the stream. Flooding threatens structures along MS
Highway 43 near the bridge and fills culverts and ditches along
bridge approach.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:45 AM CST Sunday the stage was 17.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 5:45 AM CST Sunday was 17.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.5 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.5
feet on 04/10/2021.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/lix.  Click on
the Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.

The next statement will be issued when updates are needed.

properties.areaDesc: Southwest San Juan Mountains; Four Corners/Upper Dolores River; Animas River Basin; San Juan River Basin; Southeast Utah; La Sal and Abajo Mountains; Canyonlands/Natural Bridges
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 10:37PM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and southeast
Utah, including the following areas, Canyonlands/Natural Bridges,
La Sal and Abajo Mountains and Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...From 5 AM MST Sunday through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recently burned areas, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 3 inches of rain is expected across portions of southeast
Utah and southwest Colorado from Sunday morning through Monday
morning over soils that are still saturated from recent rainfall
and flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 5 AM MST SUNDAY THROUGH MONDAY MORNING

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 31 at 9:31PM MST until November 1 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Little Colorado River Valley, Eastern Mogollon Rim, and
White Mountains.

* WHEN...From 8 AM to 11 PM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Travel
will be difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles, such as RVs, campers, and tractor trailers. Use
extra caution.

Secure loose outdoor objects that could be blown around or damaged by
the wind.

NWSheadline: WIND ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 8 AM TO 11 PM MST SUNDAY

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued October 31 at 10:50PM CDT until November 2 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Isolated minor coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Wave run-up may approach the dunes along narrow
beaches. Beach equipment, such as umbrellas and chairs, could be
moved by waves. Vehicles driving along narrow beaches may
experience higher water levels. Elevated water levels may also
occur across the Laguna Madre and South Bay, and along State
Highway 4 west of Boca Chica State Park.
properties.instruction: Do not drive through flooded roadways.

natural avalanches above treeline. Check the forecast at
